full_judgment:
Rule has been issued calling upon the opposite party to show cause as to why the judgment and decree dated 8-7-2019 passed by the Additional District Judge, 6th Court, Dhaka, in Family Appeal No.247 of 2017, affirming those dated 24-8-2017 passed by the learned Additional Assistant Judge and Family Court, Dhaka, in Family Suit No.81 of 2016 should not be set-aside and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. The opposite party herein as plaintiff instituted the aforesaid family suit seeking decree of unpaid dower money and maintenance contending that plaintiff was married with defendant on 28-9-2010 at dower money of Taka 80,000. After leading conjugal life for one month the plaintiff came to Dhaka for job and defendant used to live in his village house. The defendant did not give maintenance to the plaintiff since 10-5-2014. The defendant also did not pay dower money of the plaintiff. On 9-10-2015 the defendant divorced the plaintiff. Hence the instant suit. 

 4. The trial Court decreed the suit in part granting dower money of Taka 80,000 and further sum of Taka 80,000 as maintenance totaling Taka 1,60,000 and directed the defendant to pay the same within 60 days. The appellate Court affirmed the judgment and decree of the trial Court and found that admittedly the defendant divorced the plaintiff on 9-10-2015. 

 "In order to obtain decree for dissolution, it must be shown that there was a legal duty on the husband to maintain his wife at the relevant time and that he failed to neglected to perform that duty. Under the Muslim Law. The wife is under an obligation to obey and carry out lawful and reasonable instructions of her husband, submit herself to him and live with him in his house her failure to do so will disentitle her to maintenance." 

 "In the present case it is clear to me on the evidence on the record that the plaintiff was neither faithful nor obedient to her husband the defendant. Plaintiff and defendant lived together for a month in the house of the plaintiff's mother. Thereafter the defendant refused to continue to live with his wife in the housed of her mother and ordered his wife to accompany him to live with him elsewhere. The plaintiff was bound to obey the behest of the husband. The husband was under no obligation whatever to discontinue to live in the house of his mother-in-law. It is in evidence that the wife refused to go with her husband. He was in these circumstances under no legal obligation to maintain her. After two years the husband instituted a suit for restitution of conjugal rights. The suit was defended and he obtained a decree for restitution of conjugal rights against the plaintiff. The plaintiff was therefore bound to go and live with her husband. There is evidence on the record that after the decree obtained by the plaintiff in suit No. 107 of 1939 the defendant with some people of the jamait approached the plaintiff and asked her to come and live with him. She refused. Under these circumstances the husband was under no obligation to maintain his wife under the general Mahomedan Law. To my mind, it is clear that at no time after the husband and wife separated was plaintiff justified in keeping away from her husband and disobeying his lawful orders, and the husband was at no time in the circumstances of the case under an obligation under Mohamedan law to support and maintain a disobedient wife, who had refused to live with him for the sole reason that he refused to live in her mother's house. The plaintiff has given some evidence about cruelty but her statement on the point is without corroboration." 

 12. Present case is aptly similar with the facts and circumstances of the aforesaid ratios. So the judgment and decrees passed by the Courts below is modified to the extent that the plaintiff will get dower money of Taka 80,000 plus Taka 12,000 as maintenance for iddat period totaling Taka 92,000. The petitioner is directed to pay the said amount with two equal installments within 3(three) months from date, in default the opposite party plaintiff will be entitled to get the amount recovered through execution and in that event the petitioner defendant will be saddled with interest @ 10% on the decreetal amount until the amount is realized.
